claims.feature: first person as natural storytelling voice
claims.claim: Hobb chooses first person because it is the voice people use when telling family what happened today.
claims.source: A Dribble of Ink interview (Aidan Moher, 2007)
claims.quote: the natural voice for the story teller

claims.claim: First person lets the reader be privy to the viewpoint character's innermost thoughts and feelings.
claims.source: A Dribble of Ink interview (Aidan Moher, 2007)
claims.quote: privy to the characters innermost thoughts and feelings

claims.feature: first-person epistemic limit and dramatic irony
claims.claim: The reader knows only what the protagonist knows, yet may see what is coming before he does.
claims.quote: see what is coming even if the main character doesn't

claims.claim: In Farseer the chapter-opening prologues exist to give the reader information the first-person narrator cannot.
claims.source: A Dribble of Ink interview (Aidan Moher, 2007)
claims.quote: little prologues at the beginning of each chapter

claims.claim: First person forbids the cutaway; everything must be learned as Fitz learns it.
claims.quote: Meanwhile, back at the castle

claims.claim: She switched to third-person multiple viewpoint in Liveship only because important events happened at once in different places.
claims.source: A Dribble of Ink interview (Aidan Moher, 2007)
claims.quote: occurring simultaneously in different places

claims.claim: A hurt, physical or emotional, becomes baggage that alters later action, and the reader drags the same baggage through the reading.
claims.source: A Dribble of Ink interview (Aidan Moher, 2007)
claims.quote: drags that same baggage through the reading

claims.claim: Other heroes' ordeals feel lesser because the event is not dwelt on and leaves no lingering change; Hobb dwells and lets it change the character.
claims.source: A Dribble of Ink interview (Aidan Moher, 2007)
claims.quote: the event is not dwelt on

claims.claim: She denies being crueller than Tolkien; first person makes the same trials feel more harrowing because they are lived from inside.
claims.source: A Dribble of Ink interview (Aidan Moher, 2007)
claims.quote: perceived as more harrowing or depressing

claims.claim: Hobb describes her own style in two words, leisurely and intimate.
claims.quote: both leisurely and intimate

claims.claim: The pacing at the start of any of her books is deliberately much slower than toward the end.
claims.quote: usually a lot slower than towards the end

claims.claim: An exciting scene lacks impact unless she has slowed down to build the ramps up to it.
claims.quote: construct the ramps up to that exciting scene

claims.claim: She spends words on details and incidents that do not move the plot because they are what make the character.
claims.quote: not directly move the plot forward but are very important

claims.feature: show what is held before it is lost (consequence device)
claims.claim: A loss registers only if the text has first shown how much the lost thing mattered; otherwise the event is a throwaway moment.
claims.quote: this event is just a throwaway moment

claims.claim: Excitement and quick pace are sometimes sacrificed for character, knowingly.
claims.quote: have to be sacrificed for character

claims.claim: For dragons to be believed, everything ordinary must match our reality, down to the hero spilling his coffee.
claims.quote: the hero spills his cup of hot coffee

claims.claim: She does not smooth life out for her characters; it is never going to be all pony rides.
claims.quote: everything is always going to be pony rides

claims.claim: She avoids the language that reaches for 'throbbing' anything.
claims.quote: his or her 'throbbing' whatever

claims.claim: To write any viewpoint she puts the character on like a coat and believes everything they believe for the duration.
claims.quote: put that character on like a coat

claims.claim: Inside any viewpoint, even the villain is wondering what is for dinner.
claims.quote: even the villain is wondering what is for dinner

claims.claim: As Hobb she sprawls in novels and knows it; her Lindholm prose is much leaner.
claims.quote: In a novel, I sprawl, and I know it

claims.claim: The Hobb voice is leisurely, with more emotion and more pausing over what characters think or feel, where Lindholm reports what happened.
claims.quote: writes in a much more leisurely manner

claims.claim: The Hobb name was created to write with a depth of feeling she did not usually indulge.
claims.quote: a depth of feeling that I didn't usually indulge

claims.claim: A story idea belongs immediately and unmistakably to one of the two voices.
claims.quote: a fairly clean dividing line

claims.feature: story equals how events affect characters
claims.claim: The story is about how events affect the characters, not about the events.
claims.quote: how the events affect the characters

claims.feature: every character main character of own story
claims.claim: Each character, villain included, is written as the main character in his own story.
claims.quote: the main character in his own story

claims.feature: vocabulary as a way of seeing
claims.claim: Characters are differentiated by vocabulary, sentence structure, slang and cadence, because word choice is a way of seeing.
claims.quote: Choice of vocabulary, it's a way of seeing things

claims.claim: How a character reacts to an event reveals more than exposition does.
claims.quote: Reaction shots reveal character

claims.claim: A believable character is shaped by the world they grew up in, not dropped into it.
claims.quote: The character has to be shaped by the world

claims.claim: In any description she tries to engage as many of the five senses as possible.
claims.quote: engage as many of them as possible

claims.claim: Magic must be scarce; three wishes make a tale, infinite wishes make none.
claims.quote: an infinite number of wishes is no story at all

claims.claim: Determine coinage and the value of money and keep it consistent through the book.
claims.quote: Determine coinage and value of money

claims.claim: Research economy and geography: a tiny village will not support an artisan specialising in doorknockers.
claims.quote: an artisan specializing in doorknockers

claims.feature: food constrained by technology, geography, climate
claims.claim: A meal must be believable for the technology level, geography and climate, and such details fall naturally into the tale.
claims.source: Fran Wilde, Cooking the Books guest post (2014)
claims.quote: the technology level, the geography and climate

claims.claim: Status registers in the ordinary: food served in the kitchen was warmer than food served in the hall.
claims.source: Fran Wilde, Cooking the Books guest post (2014)
claims.quote: warmer than that served in the hall

claims.claim: A character on the frontier has a limited menu, and the constraint is listed item by item.
claims.source: Fran Wilde, Cooking the Books guest post (2014)
claims.quote: No flour, no sugar, no milk, cream or butter

claims.feature: magic paid for in the body
claims.claim: The whole saga grew from asking what if magic were addictive and degenerative, so that power is paid for physically.
claims.quote: What if magic were addictive?

claims.claim: Magic that everybody can do becomes commonplace technology; scarcity keeps it magic.
claims.quote: any sufficiently common magic is technology

claims.claim: Violence is written to be horrifying and ugly, never lascivious, and rape as a haunting that never fully leaves.
claims.quote: how horrifying and ugly violence is

claims.claim: Once a story goes somewhere she does not turn back or undo it with an it-was-all-a-dream.
claims.quote: Follow the story, wherever it goes

claims.claim: When a character makes a stupid decision the writer is stuck with it and must write the consequence.
claims.quote: you are stuck with it

claims.claim: What happens to a character changes her permanently, and a character not shaped by her experiences makes those experiences pointless to write.
claims.quote: The things that happen to us change us

claims.claim: Physical damage must leave aftermath, bruises, blood, limping, vomiting, because a good character does not protect anyone from a concussion.
claims.quote: no one limps or throws up in the corner

claims.feature: product of what has been done to us
claims.claim: Characters become the product of what has been done to them, or for them.
claims.quote: the product of what has been done to us

claims.claim: Characters step onto the stage unplanned and are allowed their own ideas about the story; the Fool was outlined as a minor character.
claims.quote: some characters just have their own ideas about the story

claims.claim: The interviewer places Hobb's writing closer to slice-of-life than to action, with fights serving character rather than plot.
claims.quote: closer the slice-of-life style than to action

claims.claim: Her research prefers diaries, journals and other primary documents over histories.
claims.quote: diaries, journals and things of that sort

claims.claim: She booked time aboard tall ships to get the smells and sensations of a sailing vessel.
claims.quote: the smells and sensations of a sailing vessel

claims.claim: She writes from questions, not answers, and dislikes message stories.
claims.quote: I do not care for 'message' stories

claims.claim: Events in one place inevitably have repercussions elsewhere in the world.
claims.quote: inevitably have repercussions in the Six Duchies

claims.claim: She wrote one novel in first-person present tense and will never attempt it again.
claims.quote: something I will NEVER attempt again

claims.claim: She wanted the world's deep history to unfold slowly.
claims.quote: I wanted it to unfold slowly

claims.claim: Each viewpoint reports its own sensory self-interest, as a dog cares how much butter is on the popcorn.
claims.quote: how much butter is on the popcorn

claims.claim: Fitz's voice kept taking her over even in emails, which is why Tawny Man followed Liveship.
claims.quote: even when I was writing e-mails

claims.claim: Her writing log records researching diseases of sheep and inserting chapter headings as bridge scaffolding.
claims.quote: researched diseases of sheep

claims.claim: Erikson admired the controlled point of view and leisurely pace, then found it a quiet seduction that set up the dog scene.
claims.quote: the controlled point of view, the leisurely pace

claims.feature: knowledge fed at a child's pace
claims.claim: The child narrator lets world-knowledge be fed piecemeal at a child's pace of comprehension.
claims.quote: at a child's pace of comprehension

claims.feature: first person unusual in epic fantasy
claims.claim: First person is an unusual approach in epic fantasy and gives complete immersion in Fitz's personality.
claims.source: Ilana Teitelbaum, Los Angeles Review of Books (2014)
claims.quote: complete immersion in Fitz's complicated personality

claims.claim: Withywoods values handkerchiefs, beeswax candles and lace as objects, a milieu likened to the Little House books.
claims.source: Ilana Teitelbaum, Los Angeles Review of Books (2014)
claims.quote: the objects of daily life are concrete and treasured

claims.claim: Conversations turn to herbs, crop seasons and fair treatment of servants rather than battle.
claims.source: Ilana Teitelbaum, Los Angeles Review of Books (2014)
claims.quote: the uses of herbs, the seasons for crops

claims.claim: She revs the engine only in the last hundred pages, after ensconcing the reader, which multiplies payoff and heartbreak.
claims.source: Ilana Teitelbaum, Los Angeles Review of Books (2014)
claims.quote: revving the engine in the hundred pages before the end

claims.claim: The important thing between characters is what is not said.
claims.source: Ilana Teitelbaum, Los Angeles Review of Books (2014)
claims.quote: what is most important is what is not said

claims.claim: There is no magic moment of overcoming; childhood traumas linger and take new shapes as Fitz ages.
claims.source: Ilana Teitelbaum, Los Angeles Review of Books (2014)
claims.quote: no magic moment of overcoming the past

claims.claim: Magic and brutal violence are fuel for the psychological dimension, not the other way around.
claims.source: Ilana Teitelbaum, Los Angeles Review of Books (2014)
claims.quote: fuel for the psychological dimension

claims.claim: The early Farseer volumes are couched as a painfully confessional memoir presented as a manuscript for future perusal.
claims.quote: painfully confessional memoir

claims.claim: Langford finds the reader feels every blow, sword-cut and fever.
claims.quote: You feel every blow, sword-cut and fever suffered

claims.claim: How Fitz reacts to things is the story; four-fifths of a book can be tea and clothes and remain the best part.
claims.source: Vacuous Wastrel review of Fool's Assassin (2014)
claims.quote: how Fitz reacts to things is the story

claims.claim: Even when Fitz is calm and happy the prose shows him working hard to stay so.
claims.source: Vacuous Wastrel review of Fool's Assassin (2014)
claims.quote: even when Fitz is calm and happy

claims.claim: Fitz's prose feels natural because it is intimate, but its clarity is literary intelligence, not simplicity.
claims.source: The Huntress and the Wolf (Substack essay)
claims.quote: intimacy should not be mistaken for simplicity

claims.claim: Fitz narrates his doubts, failures, grief and shame while his competence passes without comment.
claims.source: The Huntress and the Wolf (Substack essay)
claims.quote: his doubts, failures, grief, and shame

claims.claim: Character is shown through inventories of the mundane on the mantel and the desk.
claims.source: The Huntress and the Wolf (Substack essay)
claims.quote: medicinal unguents on the mantel, two pens at the ready

claims.claim: Characters are so real that readers stay fascinated even while they perform the most routine tasks.
claims.quote: even when they are performing the most routine tasks

claims.claim: A sympathetic critic finds overreliance on adverbs stunts the Liveship novels' flow.
claims.quote: overreliance on adverbs often stunts the novel's flow

claims.feature: loss as what is not received
claims.claim: Loss is rendered through what Fitz does not get, and compressed with 'After a time'.
claims.source: Jeffrey David Outcalt, Substack close reading
claims.quote: no princess saved, no true love

claims.claim: She never shies from the exhausting reality of traveling, hunting and dealing with other people.
claims.quote: the exhausting reality of traveling, hunting, dealing with other people

claims.claim: A reader of The Inheritance finds Hobb epic and Lindholm more to the point.
claims.quote: Lindholm writes more to the point

claims.claim: Readers report the books are lived rather than read.
claims.quote: you don't so much read them as live them
